ORDER On July 12, 2017, complainant through counsel, filed a “REPLY WITH MOTION TO DECLARE DEFENDANT IN DEFAULT” alleging that the Answer , submitted by respondent, People’s General Insurance Corporation is invalid for - failing to indicate the authority of Mr. Luisito C. Aragon, Senior Adjuster of respondent's Claims Department, to sign and submit the Answer for and in behalf of the respondent insurance company. , On July 26, 2017, respondent through counsel, filed an “OPPOSITION TO . . MOTION TO DECLARE RESPONDENT IN DEFAULT WITH REJOINDER” : accompanied by a Certification from the Assistant Corporate Secretary of the respondent to prove that Mr. Luisito C. Aragon is duly authorized to act for and in behalf of the respondent. It also avers that the Rules of Procedure Governing Trial and Hearing of Claim Cases on Insurance does not require that the same be verified. ; On August 9, 2017, this Commission received from the complainant a “REPLY RE: COMMENT/OPPOSITION DATED JULY 21, 2017” contending that the - ’ belated Certification did not cure the jurisdictional defect because it did not state the date of the alleged special meeting or the number of directors who approved the . resolution appointing Mr. Luisito C. Aragon as representative of the respondent. ) Thus, the issue to be resolved is: whether or not respondent should be declared in default. : After a careful review, this Commission resolves to deny complainant's Motion to Declare Defendant's in Default. Considering that respondent has attached _ to its Opposition, a Certification from the Assistant Corporate Secretary, which *. states, in part: . , . “3. At the special meeting of the Board of Directors of the Corporation held at its : principal office, at which a quorum was present and acted throughout, the following . resolutions were duly approved and recorded in the MINUTES OF THE BOARD MEETING;” : IC-LCA-DP-001-T-07 4 0 | 1020058 ~—g/p . a. ’ . , . . Xxx a , ; , “RESOLVED, that MR.LUISITO C, ARAGON, Senior Claims Adjuster, .be authorized to act for and in behalf of the corporation in filing, initiating and defending all cases in all courts or administrative agencies filed for or against or * involving any right or interest of People's General Insurance Corporation.” « : ae The Supreme Court, in several cases, has recognized the sufficiency of a Secretary's Certificate as proof of authority for an individual named in it to represent a corporation in a suit’. , Thus, the subsequent submission of a Certification, attesting that the signatory, Mr. Luis C. Aragon, was authorized to represent for and in behalf of the respondent insurance company is sufficient to prove his authority and representation. Asimple perusal of the records shows that the Certification from the Assistant - ~ Secretary was executed on June 22, 2017 while the Answer was also executed and filed on June 22, 2017. Clearly then, Mr. Luis C. Aragon, was duly authorized to sign the verification and that a Secretary's Certificate is sufficient proof of said authority. Moreover, application of technical rules of procedure may be relaxed to serve the demands of substantial justice. Thus, procedural lapses such as in the case at bar, must be disregarded to be able to fully hear the case and properly determine the insurance claim of the complainant. ’ Well-settled is the rule that courts should be liberal in setting aside orders of default for default judgments are frowned upon, unless in cases where it clearly appears that the reopening of the case is intended for delay. The issuance of orders of default should be the exception rather than the rule, to be allowed only in clear cases of obstinate refusal by the defendant to comply with the orders of the trial - court. Suits should as much as possible be decided on the merits and not on technicalities?. IN VIEW OF THE FOREGOING, complainant's Motion to Declare Defendant in Default is hereby DENIED. Request for Full Admittance of Investment made in Northwest Insurance & Surety Co., Inc.’s (NISCO); . . 2. Request for Comment/Feedback on the CTPL Proposal of AA Guaranty Assurance Co., Inc.; and 3. Compliance with the P550 Million Networth Requirement Dear Mr. Co, . This pertains to the following letters, to wit: ‘ 1. Letter dated June 23, 2017 requesting for the full admittance of Reliance . Surety & Insurance Co., Inc.'s (RSICI) investment in NISCO through the acquisition of Ninety Two Percent (92%) of the outstanding common stock of NISCO equivalent to Two Million Four Hundred Ninety Nine ; Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Seven (2,499,997) shares and Comment/Feedback on the CTPL Proposal of AA Guaranty Assurance Co., Inc.; . 2. Letter dated August 1, 2017 outlining the response of RSICI's . management to the result of the verification of RSICI's 2016 Annual Statement; and . 3. Letter dated August 2, 2017 outlining the response of NISCO's ; management's response to the result of the verification of NISCO's 2016 Annual Statement. [702 00° 983 | shy Head Office: P.O. Box 3589 Manila FAX No.522-14-34 Tel. Nos. 523-84-61 to 70 Website: www.insurance.gov.ph 1 |. REQUEST FOR FULL ADMITTANCE OF INVESTMENT MADE IN NISCO BACKGROUND : It will be recalled that on September 17, 2015, this Commission received a letter from RSICI informing the Commission that its Letter of Intent for the acquisition of the entire assets and business portfolio and assumption of all liabilities of : NISCO had been accepted by NISCO, through its President, Ms. Olivia N. Ang. After evaluation of the proposed transaction, the Insurance Commission, in a letter dated October 26, 2015, acknowledged RSICI's letter and advised the parties that the proposed transaction between RSICI and NISCO will be ‘ considered a merger and reminded the parties to comply with the requirements under IC Circular Letter No. 2015-11 dated March 18, 2015, which provides the Rules and Regulations on Consolidation and Merger of Insurance Companies. Subsequently, on December 7, 2015, this Commission received a letter from RSICI acknowledging the October 26, 2015 letter issued by this Commission and at the same time, manifesting that they will no longer proceed with the proposed acquisition of the entire assets and business portfolio and assumption of all liabilities of NISCO. Instead, the parties will enter into a share purchase agreement wherein RSICI will buy One Hundred Percent (100%) of NISCO's outstanding common stock. Another letter dated December 28, 2015 was sent by RSICI informing the Commission that they have already finalized the acquisition of Ninety Two Percent (92%) of NISCO's outstanding common stock. Thereafter, NISCO will cease to write new risks and will be on a run-off basis and will operate independently from RSICI. Afterwards, the portfolio of NISCO will be transferred to RSICI as the respective policies expire. In a meeting held on March 11, 2016, RSICI and NISCO were informed that the transaction required the prior approval of this Commission as an investment subject to the limitation found under Sec. 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended. NISCO was also informed that it must apply for a servicing license since NISCO will be in a state of run-off in accordance with IC Circular Letter | No, 2014-14. In compliance with the above-mentioned directives, RSICI sent a letter dated March 18, 2016 requesting for the approval of the acquisition by RSICI of Ninety Two Percent (92%) of the outstanding common stock of NISCO equivalent to Two Million Four Hundred Ninety Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Seven (2,499,997) shares. On April 22, 2016, NISCO applied for a servicing license in accordance with the agreement during the March 11, 2016 meeting. 2 . In a letter dated May 24, 2016, this Commission advised RSICI that the company may invest only up to Php50,000,000.00 as provided under Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, equivalent to Twenty Percent (20%) of NISCO’'s latest verified networth. RSICI was also informed that any amount in excess of the limitation shall be considered as non-admitted asset and reminded to make the necessary cash infusion should there be any deficiency in its minimum networth requirement in the future. ; In a letter dated June 5, 2016, RSICI asked for reconsideration in the manner of applying Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, by applying the ; twenty percent (20%) limitation in investment to the networth of RSICI, instead of the paid-up capital of NISCO. On July 13, 2016, this Commission received another letter from RSICI manifesting that it has decided to convert NISCO’s application for a servicing license into a regular license and is requesting reconsideration that the entire value of its investment be approved. According to RSICI, they have decided to convert the application for license into a regular license to attract additional investors and in complying with the networth requirement. Furthermore, to support its request for reconsideration, RSIC!] argued that limiting the admittance of its investment in NISCO is detrimental to its capital build-up program and brings about solvency concerns. On July 22, 2016, RSICI sent another letter in relation to NISCO’s application for a regular license. RSICI manifested that once the regular license is released, they will operate NiISCO with the view of attracting strategic investors made up of motor car dealers to purchase the common shares of NISCO with RSICI maintaining up to twenty percent (20%) interest and manage the company on behalf of the investors. RSICI also manifested that NISCO has been a regular member of insurance pools which they would like to maintain for the year 2016, which will generate an estimated volume of Php25,000,000.00 in inward business. However, in order to receive the income, NISCO must have a regular license by the end of July 2016. On August 15, 2016, this Commission partially approved RSICI's request for reconsideration subject to the following terms and conditions, to wit: 1. The request for reconsideration in relation to the manner of applying Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, was granted. : ; Thus, instead of using the paid-up capital of NISCO as basis in , determining the twenty percent (20%) limitation under Section 211 of the Amended Insurance Code, the networth of RSICI was used as basis. As a result, the amount of investment to be admitted as an asset of RSICI was increased from Php50,000,000.00 to ; Php123,164.945.14; 2. RSICI and NISCO were further required to submit the following documents within thirty (30) days from receipt of the August 15, 2016 letter: 3 a. Documents to support the acquisition of NISCO pursuant to IC Circular Letter No. 2014-37 dated 05 September 2014; | b. Copy of the Certificate Authorizing Registration (CAR) issued by the Bureau of Internal Revenue; and c. Notarized undertaking executed by the President/COO of RSICI to comply with the Php550 Million networth requirement by the end of the year 2016. The same notarized undertaking was required of NISCO. 3. The request to consider the entire value of the investment made in the purchase of NISCO’s common shares of stock as an admitted asset was denied for being moot and academic (Emphasis supplied); and, 4, NISCO's application for a regular license was granted subject to the conduct of an examination in order to verify if NISCO is compliant with the networth requirement for the year ending 2015. On September 30, 2016 and December 21, 2016, RSICI partially complied with the submission of documentary requirements under IC Circular Letter No. 2014-37 dated 05 September 2014 and, at the same time, requested for the full admittance of RSICI's investment in NISCO. ll. ON THE REQUEST FOR RECONSIDERATION FOR FULL ADMITTANCE OF RSICI’S INVESTMENT IN NISCO Please be informed that this Commission hereby denies your request for the full admittance of RSICI's investment in NISCO. Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, provides that: "SEC. 211. After satisfying the requirements contained in Sections 197, 199, 209 and 210, any non-life insurance company may invest any portion of its funds tepresenting earned surplus in any of the investments described in Sections 204, 206 and 207, or in any securities issued by a registered enterprise mentioned in the preceding sections: Provided, That no Investment in stocks or bonds of any single entity shall in the aggregate, exceed twenty percent (20%) of the net | worth of the Insurance company as shown in its latest financial statement approved by the Commissioner _or twenty percent (20%) of the paid-up capltal_of the issuing company, whichever is lesser, unless otherwise approved by the Commissioner.” (Emphasis supplied) It must be emphasized that under Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, this Commission has no discretion as to the amount of limitation in investment in securities by a non-life insurance company. The twenty percent (20%) limitation is fixed by law which cannot be breached without violating the above-quoted provision. Also, the phrase “unless otherwise approved by the Commissioner” pertains to the discretion given to the Insurance Commissioner as to whether the twenty 4 percent (20%) limitation will be applied to the net worth of the insurance company or the paid-up capital of the issuing company. Clearly, this discretion does not pertain to whether or not Investment in securities may exceed the twenty percent (20%) limitation. Lastly, it must be pointed out that both RSICI and NISCO, through its Presiden/COO, submitted a notarized undertaking to comply with the Php550 Million networth requirement by the end of 2016 and committed to infuse additional capital in the event of deficiency. . Thus, your request for the full admittance of RSICI's investment in NISCO is , hereby denied with finality. il, ON THE REQUEST FOR COMMENT/FEEDBACK ON THE CTPL , PROPOSAL OF AA GUARANTY ASSURANCE CO., INC. Considering that the proposed CTPL program was not supported by the industry, through the Philippine Insurers and Reinsurers Association, Inc. (PIRA), this Commission cannot support and sanction the proposed CTPL program. Also, while the objectives and goals of the program are laudable, to allow the same wherein only one insurance company will issue all Compulsory Third Party Liability insurance policies is to promote monopoly and restraint of trade which is prohibited under the 1887 Constitution and the Philippine Competition Act of 2016. IV. ON THE COMPLIANCE WITH THE PHP550 MILLION NET WORTH REQUIREMENT RESULT OF THE VERIFICATION OF RSICI'S 2016 ANNUAL STATEMENT Based on this Commission's verification of RSICI's Annual Statement for the year ending December 31, 2016, RSICI has a net worth of Php464,287, 118.67, which is deficient for the Php550 Million net worth requirement by Php85,712,881.33. The result showed that the investment of RSICI in NISCO’s common shares of stock in the amount of Php350,000,000.00, more or less, was deemed a non- admitted asset since NISCO, the issuing company of the purchased shares, was already a non-operating company with net worth deficiencies in the year 2016. Thus, to protect the interests of the policyholders and the insuring public in general, this Commission deemed it necessary to disallow the full amount of RSICI's investment in NISCO until such time that the latter has returned to its : regular business operations and has addressed its net worth deficiency. , | l 5 wt oo ‘ . On August 1, 2017, RSICI outlined its response to the results of the verification made on its 2016 Annual Statement, with some issues pertaining to the following: a. Financial Condition - RSICI's networth deficiency was mainly brought about by the complete disallowance of its investment in NISCO in the amount of Php304,999,634.00. The reason for the total non-admittance relates to NISCO’s networth deficiency. RSICI, as the majority stockholder of NISCO, infused additional capital in the amount of Php246,073,496.32. Thus, RSICI is ; requesting for the credit back of the previously approved asset in the amount of Php123,164,945.15 since NISCO is now compliant with the networth requirement. b. Offsetting of Cash Dividends to Deposit for Future Subscription — Reliance Ventures & Resources, Inc. (RVRI), the majority stockholder of RSICI, received cash dividends in the amount of , Php 99,700,000.00 on November 28, 2016 based on the audited financial statements of 2015. However, on different dates, RVRI made several deposits for future subscription with RSICI in the total amount of Php380,500,000.00. Thus, RSICI is requesting that the amount of cash dividends ordered by this Commission to be returned be offset to the Deposit for Future Subscription made by RVRI. It must be emphasized that the fact that the infusion of additional capital made by an insurance company arose out of an order or directive by this Commission does not mean that the requirements of prior approval and the limitation on investments can be dispensed with. Thus, RSICI is directed to submit the necessary request for approval in investments with the Investment Services Division of this Commission and to pay the appropriate fine for fallure to seek the prior approval of this Commission. The request for credit back of the previously approved asset in the amount of Php123,164,945.15 will be considered for evaluation once RSICI has complied with the above-mentioned directive and NISCO has secured a regular license from this Commission. As to the request for offsetting of the cash dividends received by RVRI ordered by this Commission to be returned from RVRI’s Deposit for future subscription, the same is hereby denied. Under the rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), a corporation should not consider a deposit for future subscription unless the following elements are present: “(1) The unissued authorized capital stock of the entity is insufficient to cover the amount of shares indicated in the contract; 6 . ty * , , c ' (2) There is Board of Directors’ approval on the proposed increase in authorized capital stock (for which a deposit was received by the corporation); (3) There is stockholders’ approval of said proposed increase; and (4) The application for the approval of the proposed increase has been filed with the Commission. It_is_ understood from the foregoing that there is a subscription agreement which, among other things, states that the corporation is not contractually obliged to return the consideration received and that the corporation is obliged to deliver a fixed number of its own shares of stock for a fixed amount of cash or property paid or to be paid by the contracting party.” Based on the foregoing, if the requested offsetting is approved and executed, the same will render nugatory RSICI’s compliance with the SEC requirements since it is specifically required that the corporation is not contractually obliged : to return the consideration received. | RESULT OF THE VERIFICATION OF NISCO’S 2016 ANNUAL STATEMENT Based on this Commission's verification of NISCO’s Annual Statement for the year ending December 31, 2016, NISCO has a net worth of Php304,899,290.16, which is deficient for the Php550 Million net worth requirement by Php245, 100,709.84. On August 2, 2017, NISCO manifested that its majority stockholder, RSICI, has infused additional capital in the amount of Php218,500,000.00 to cover up its networth deficiency. Please be advised, however, that this Commission will only consider for ; evaluation the infusion of additional capital by RSICI once it has submitted its request for approval of investment with this Commission. | Once approved, NISCO should apply for the issuance of a regular license since it currently holding a servicing license. Compliance with the P550 Million Networth Requirement Dear Mr. Co, This pertains to the following letters, to wit: 1. Letter dated June 23, 2017 requesting for the full admittance of Reliance Surety & Insurance Co., Inc.’s (RSICI) investment in NISCO through the acquisition of Ninety Two Percent (92%) of the outstanding common stock of NISCO equivalent to Two Million Four Hundred Ninety Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Seven (2,499,997) shares and Comment/Feedback on the CTPL. Nos, 523-84-61 to 70 Website: www.insurance.gov.ph : bay ! I. REQUEST FOR FULL ADMITTANCE OF INVESTMENT MADE IN NISCO BACKGROUND : It will be recalled that on September 17, 2015, this Commission received a letter from RSICI informing the Commission that its Letter of Intent for the acquisition of the entire assets and business portfolio and assumption of all liabilities of NISCO had been accepted by NISCO, through its President, Ms. Olivia N. Ang. After evaluation of the proposed transaction, the Insurance Commission, in a letter dated October 26, 2015, acknowledged RSICI’s letter and advised the parties that the proposed transaction between RSICI and NISCO will be . considered a merger and reminded the parties to comply with the requirements under IC Circular Letter No. 2015-11 dated March 18, 2015, which provides the Rules and Regulations on Consolidation and Merger of Insurance Companies. Subsequently, on December 7, 2015, this Commission received a letter from RSICI acknowledging the October 26, 2015 letter Issued by this Commission and at the same time, manifesting that they will no longer proceed with the proposed acquisition of the entire assets and business portfolio and assumption of all liabilities of NISCO. Instead, the parties will enter into a share purchase agreement wherein RSICI will buy One Hundred Percent (100%) of NISCO’s outstanding common stock. Another letter dated December 28, 2015 was sent by RSICI informing the Commission that they have already finalized the acquisition of Ninety Two Percent (92%) of NISCO's outstanding common stock. Thereafter, NISCO will cease to write new risks and will be on a run-off basis and will operate independently from RSICI. Afterwards, the portfolio of NISCO will be transferred to RSICI as the respective policies expire. In a meeting held on March 11, 2016, RSICI and NISCO were informed that the transaction required the prior approval of this Commission as an investment subject to the limitation found under Sec. 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended. NISCO was also informed that it must apply for a servicing license since NISCO will be in a state of run-off in accordance with IC Circular Letter No. 2014-14. In compliance with the above-mentioned directives, RSICI sent a letter dated March 18, 2016 requesting for the approval of the acquisition by RSICI of Ninety Two Percent (92%) of the outstanding common stock of NISCO equivalent to Two Million Four Hundred Ninety Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Ninety Seven (2,499,997) shares. ' On April 22, 2016, NISCO applied for a servicing license in accordance with the agreement during the March 11, 2016 meeting. 2 ‘ In a letter dated May 24, 2016, this Commission advised RSICI that the company may invest only up to Php50,000,000.00 as provided under Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, equivalent to Twenty Percent (20%) of NISCO’s latest verified networth. RSICI was also informed that any amount : in excess of the limitation shall be considered as non-admitted asset and reminded to make the necessary cash infusion should there be any deficiency in its minimum networth requirement in the future. In a letter dated June 5, 2016, RSICI asked for reconsideration in the manner of applying Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, by applying the ; twenty percent (20%) limitation in investment to the networth of RSICI, instead of the paid-up capital of NISCO. On July 13, 2016, this Commission received another letter from RSICI manifesting that it has decided to convert NISCO's application for a servicing license into a regular license and is requesting reconsideration that the entire value of its investment be approved. According to RSICI, they have decided to convert the application for license into a regular license to attract additional investors and in complying with the networth requirement. Furthermore, to support its request for reconsideration, RSIC! argued that limiting the admittance of its investment in NISCO is detrimental to its capital build-up program and brings about solvency concerns. On July 22, 2016, RSICI sent another letter in relation to NISCO’s application for a regular license. RSIC! manifested that once the regular license is released, they will operate NISCO with the view of attracting strategic investors made up of motor car dealers to purchase the common shares of NISCO with RSICI maintaining up to twenty percent (20%) interest and manage the company on behalf of the investors. RSICI also manifested that NISCO has been a regular member of insurance pools which they would like to maintain for the year 2016, which will generate an estimated volume of Php25,000,000.00 in inward business, However, in order to receive the income, NISCO must have a regular license by the end of July 2016. On August 15, 2016, this Commission partially approved RSICI's request for reconsideration subject to the following terms and conditions, to wit: 1. The request for reconsideration in relation to the manner of applying | Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, was granted. ; Thus, instead of using the paid-up capital of NISCO as basis in determining the twenty percent (20%) limitation under Section 211 of the Amended Insurance Code, the networth of RSIC! was used as basis. As a result, the amount of investment to be admitted as an asset of RSIC! was: increased from Php50,000,000.00 to , Php123,164.945.14; 2. RSICI and NISCO were further required to submit the following documents within thirty (30) days from receipt of the August 15, 2016 letter: 3 a, Documents to support the acquisition of NISCO pursuant to IC Circular Letter No. 2014-37 dated 05 September 2014; b. Copy of the Certificate Authorizing Registration (CAR) issued by the Bureau of Internal Revenue; and c. Notarized undertaking executed by the President/COO of RSICI to comply with the Php550 Million networth requirement by the end of the year 2016. The same notarized undertaking was required of NiSCO. 3. The request to consider the entire value of the investment made in the purchase of NISCO’s common shares of stock as an admitted : asset was denied for being moot and academic (Emphasis supplied); and, . 4, NISCO's application for a regular license was granted subject to the conduct of an examination in order to verify if NISCO is compliant with the networth requirement for the year ending 2015. On September 30, 2016 and December 21, 2016, RSICI partially complied with the submission of documentary requirements under IC Circular Letter No. 2014-37 dated 05 September 2014 and, at the same time, requested for the full admittance of RSICI's investment in NISCO, Il. ON THE REQUEST FOR RECONSIDERATION FOR FULL ADMITTANCE OF RSICI’S INVESTMENT IN NISCO Please be informed that this Commission hereby denies your request for the full admittance of RSICI’s investment in NISCO. Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as amended, provides that: “SEC. 211. After satisfying the requirements contained in Sections 197, 199, 209 and 210, any non-life insurance company may Invest any portion of its funds representing earned surplus in any of the investments described in Sections 204, 206 and 207, or in any securities issued by a registered enterprise mentioned in the preceding sections: Provided, That no investment in stocks or bonds of any single entity shall In the aqqreqate, exceed twenty percent (20%) of the net | worth of the insurance company as shown in its latest financlal statement approved by the Commissioner or twenty percent (20%) of the pald-up | capital_of the issuing company, whichever Is lesser, unless otherwise approved by the Commissioner.” (Emphasis supplied} It must be emphasized that under Section 211 of the Insurance Code, as i amended, this Commission has no discretion as to the amount of limitation in investment in securities by a non-life insurance company. The twenty percent (20%) limitation is fixed by law which cannot be breached without violating the above-quoted provision. Also, the phrase “unless otherwise approved by the Commissioner’ pertains to the discretion given to the Insurance Commissioner as to whether the twenty 4 percent (20%) limitation will be applied to the net worth of the insurance company or the paid-up capital of the issuing company. Clearly, this discretion does not pertain to whether or not investment in securities may exceed the twenty percent (20%) limitation. Lastly, it must be pointed out that both RSICI and NISCO, through its President/(COO, submitted a notarized undertaking to comply with the Php550 Million networth requirement by the end of 2016 and committed to infuse additional capltal in the event of deficiency. ; Thus, your request for the full admittance of RSICI’s investment in NISCO is hereby denied with finality. Ill, ON THE REQUEST FOR COMMENT/FEEDBACK ON THE CTPL PROPOSAL OF AA GUARANTY ASSURANCE CO., INC. | Considering that the proposed CTPL program was not supported by the industry, through the Philippine Insurers and Reinsurers Association, Inc. (PIRA), this Commission cannot support and sanction the proposed CTPL program. Also, while the objectives and goals of the program are laudable, to allow the same wherein only one insurance company will issue all Compulsory Third Party Liability insurance policies is to promote monopoly and restraint of trade which is prohibited under the 1987 Constitution and the Philippine Competition Act of 2016. IV. ON THE COMPLIANCE WITH THE PHP550 MILLION NET WORTH REQUIREMENT RESULT OF THE VERIFICATION OF RSICI’S 2016 ANNUAL STATEMENT Based on this Commission's verification of RSICI's Annual Statement for the year ending December 31, 2016, RSICI has a net worth of Php464,287,118.67, which is deficient for the Php550 Million net worth requirement by Php85,712,881.33. The result showed that the investment of RSICI in NISCO's common shares of stock in the amount of Php350,000,000.00, more or less, was deemed a non- admitted asset since NISCO, the issuing company of the purchased shares, was already a non-operating company with net worth deficiencies in the year 2016. Thus, to protect the interests of the policyholders and the insuring public in general, this Commission deemed it necessary to disallow the full amount of RSICI's investment in NISCO until such time that the latter has returned to its ' regular business operations and has addressed its net worth deficiency. | | | | 5 | | ’ On August 1, 2017, RSICI outlined its response to the results of the verification made on its 2016 Annual Statement, with some issues pertaining to the following: a. Financial Condition — RSICI's networth deficiency was mainly brought about by the complete disallowance of its investment in NISCO in the amount of Php304,999,634.00. The reason for the total non-admittance relates to NISCO's networth deficiency. RSICI, as the majority stockholder of NISCO, infused additional capital in the amount of Php246,073,496.32. Thus, RSICI is requesting for the credit back of the previously approved asset in the amount of Php123,164,945.15 since NISCO is now compliant with the networth requirement. b. Offsetting of Cash Dividends to Deposit for Future Subscription — Reliance Ventures & Resources, Inc. (RVRI), the majority stockholder of RSICI, received cash dividends in the amount of ‘ Php 99,700,000.00 on November 28, 2016 based on the audited financial statements of 2015. However, on different dates, RVRI made several deposits for future subscription with RSICI in the total amount of Php380,500,000.00. Thus, RSICI is requesting that the amount of cash dividends ordered by this Commission to be returned be offset to the Deposit for Future Subscription made by RVRI. It must be emphasized that the fact that the infusion of additional capital made by an insurance company arose out of an order or directive by this Commission does not mean that the requirements of prior approval and the limitation on investments can be dispensed with. Thus, RSICI is directed to submit the necessary request for approval in investments with the Investment Services Division of this Commission and to pay the appropriate fine for failure to seek the prior approval of this Commission. The request for credit back of the previously approved asset in the amount of Php123,164,945.15 will be considered for evaluation once RSICI has complied with the above-mentioned directive and NISCO has secured a regular license from this Commission. As to the request for offsetting of the cash dividends received by RVRI ordered by this Commission to be returned from RVRI’s Deposit for future subscription, the same is hereby denled. Under the rules of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), a corporation should not consider a deposit for future subscription unless the following elements are present: "(1) The unissued authorized capital stock of the entity is insufficient to cover the amount of shares indicated in the contract; 6 if (2) There is Board of Directors’ approval on the proposed increase in authorized capital stock (for which a deposit was received by the corporation); (3) There is stockholders’ approval of said proposed increase; and (4) The application for the approval of the proposed increase has been filed with the Commission. It_is_ understood from the foregoing that there is a subscription agreement which, among other things, states that the corporation is not contractually obliged to return the consideration received and that the corporation is obliged to deliver a fixed number of its own shares of stock for a fixed amount of cash or property paid or to be paid by the contracting party.” Based on the foregoing, if the requested offsetting is approved and executed, the same will render nugatory RSICI’s compliance with the SEC requirements since itis specifically required that the corporation is not contractually obliged i to return the consideration received. RESULT OF THE VERIFICATION OF NISCO’S 2016 ANNUAL STATEMENT Based on this Commission's verification of NISCO’s Annual Statement for the year ending December 31, 2016, NISCO has a net worth of Php304,899,290.16, which is deficient for the Php550 Million net worth requirement by Php245, 100,709.84. On August 2, 2017, NISCO manifested that its majority stockholder, RSICI, has infused additional capital in the amount of Php218,500,000.00 to cover up its networth deficiency. Please be advised, however, that this Commission will only consider for ; evaluation the infusion of additional capital by RSICI once it has submitted its request for approval of investment with this Commission. | Once approved, NISCO should apply for the issuance of a regular license since it currently holding a servicing license. On July 26, 2017, respondent through counsel, filed an “OPPOSITION TO MOTION TO DECLARE RESPONDENT IN DEFAULT WITH REJOINDER’” accompanied by a Certification from the Assistant Corporate Secretary of the respondent to prove that Mr. Luisito C. Aragon is duly authorized to act for and in behalf of the respondent. It also avers that the Rules of Procedure Governing Trial and Hearing of Claim Cases on Insurance does not require that the same be verified. On August 9, 2017, this Commission received from the complainant a “REPLY RE: COMMENT/OPPOSITION DATED JULY 21, 2017” contending thatthe belated Certification did not cure the jurisdictional defect because it did not state the date of the alleged special meeting or the number of directors who approved the resolution appointing Mr. Luisito C. Aragon as representative of the respondent. ° Thus, the issue to be resolved is: whether or not respondent should be declared in default. After a careful review, this Commission resolves to deny complainant's Motion to Declare Defendant's in Default. Considering that respondent has attached to its Opposition, a Certification from the Assistant Corporate Secretary, which states, in part: Xxx “3. At the special meeting of the Board of Directors of the Corporation held at its principal office, at which a quorum was present and acted throughout, the following resolutions were duly approved and recorded in the MINUTES OF THE BOARD MEETING;” Yor IC-LCA-DP-001-T-07 £70 A005E12 4 | Py) Xxx . “RESOLVED, that MR.LUISITO C. ARAGON, Senior Claims Adjuster, be authorized to act for and in behalf of the corporation in filing, initiating and defending all cases in all courts or administrative agencies filed for or against or involving any right or interest of People’s General Insurance Corporation.” The Supreme Court, in several cases, has recognized the sufficiency of a Secretary’s Certificate as proof of authority for an individual named in it to represent a corporation in a suit'. Thus, the subsequent submission of a Certification, attesting that the signatory, Mr. Luis C. Aragon, was authorized to represent for and in behalf of the respondent insurance company is sufficient to prove his authority and : representation. Asimple perusal of the records shows that the Certification from the Assistant Secretary was executed on June 22, 2017 while the Answer was also executed and filed on June 22, 2017. : Clearly then, Mr. Luis C, Aragon, was duly authorized to sign the verification and that a Secretary's Certificate is sufficient proof of said authority. Moreover, application of technical rules of procedure may be relaxed to serve the demands of substantial justice. Thus, procedural lapses such as in the case at bar, must be disregarded to be able to fully hear the case and properly determine the insurance claim of the complainant. Well-settled is the rule that courts should be liberal in setting aside orders of default for default judgments are frowned upon, unless in cases where it clearly appears that the reopening of the case is intended for delay. The issuance of orders of default should be the exception rather than the rule, to be allowed only in clear cases of obstinate refusal by the defendant to comply with the orders of the trial court. Suits should as much as possible be decided on the merits and not on technicalities?. IN VIEW OF THE FOREGOING, complainant's Motion to Declare Defendant in Default is hereby DENIED. SO ORDERED. The last license issued to Starcare is for July 22, 2004-July 21, 2005.1 We also note that it has no pending application filed before the IC. Under the Administrative Code of 1987, the DOH is mandated to regulate the opérations of and issue licenses and permits to hospitals, clinics, dispensaries,/and other establishments, including HMOs.? Accordingly, the DOH issued clearanceg to HMOs for them to be able to operate and sell HMO products to the public. By the issuance of Executive Order No. 192, Series of 2015, such“authority to regulate was transferred from DOH to IC. The transfer of regulation includes the authority to issue rules and regulations with respect to the establishment of HM‘minimum capitalization, net worth, reserve funds and security deposit requirements and to approve, amend, renew, decline, suspend or revoke any license issued in va of HMOs‘. It must be emphasized that since July 22, 2005 until | August 2016, Starcare had been engaged in the business of HMO without the required license from the DOH and eventually from the IC. / Furthermore, Executive Order No. 192, that was jSsued on November 12, 2015, expressly required all HMOs to comply with the regulatory requirements of procuring a License to Operate from the ICS, / Despite being fully aware of the transfer of‘regulation and concomitant obligation to apply for or renew its License to Operate, Starcare continued its operation albeit lack of necessary license from the Regulator concerned. Moreover, this requirement to procure a License to Operate, under the Administrative Code of 1987, DOH Rules and Eyecutve Order no. 192, is amplified by the issuance of IC Circular Letter No. 2015-60 entitled Guidelines in the Renewal of HMO Clearance to Operate/Licenses Expiring on’31 December 2015, which expressly provides for the renewal of clearance issued by the DOH. Again, we note that this was issued on December 23, 2015 or a month after the issuance of Executive Order No. 192, Series of 2015. By the aforesaid Gtrcular, all HMOs were reminded to procure the necessary license before they W/ ct their business. It bears stressing that since July 22, 2005, it was incumbent upon Starcare to renew its License to Operate’from the DOH before it could operate and sell its products to the public. This duty continued even after the regulation has been transferred to IC. DOF Building, Roxas Boulevard corner Pablo Ocampo, Sr. Street Manila SUBJECT: Proposed Philippine Catastrophe Insurance Pool | Dear Assistant Secretary Alvarez: This refers to the proposed Philippine Catastrophe Insurance Pool (PCIP) prepared by the National Reinsurance’ Corporation of the Philippines (NatRe), which was referred to us for comment. 1. Operational Structure While we do not object to the proposal of NatRe that the PCIP will have an organizational structure as a mutual insurance company, we prefer if it is possible that the structure shall be of a corporation where the shareholders are the insurance companies and the government, such as the Government Service Insurance System, is a minority shareholder. !n a mutual insurance company, the owners of the corporation will be the policyholders of the pool, which may bring the following disadvantages: 1. The policyholders are not as interested than the insurance companies in the governance and administration of the corporation; 2. The policyholders are not expected to provide the necessary capital In the initial stage of the corporation and in maintaining its solvency; and 3. Long and costly decision making process is inherent in the mutual company since major changes may need approval from the numerous owners of the company. ~~~ Head Oiffice; P.O, Box 3589 Manila FAX No. 522-14-34 Tel. Nos. 52-64-61 to 70 Website: wwwinsurancegovph { oben hy | “a . . . . t : . ry While the Insurance Code provides for the administration and governance of the mutual life insurance company, it does not provide for a mutual non-life insurance company. i In case a corporation is created for the PCIP to operate, the corporation is required to be licensed and supervised by the Insurance Commission under the Insurance Code, unless a law shall be passed creating the catastrophe insurance pool corporation and giving it specific powers and providing independence from regulation by the Insurance Commission. On the proposal by NatRe that the operational management of the PCIP be : outsourced to a service company, we support the idea subject to the retention of : some Important functions, which under the Insurance Code the insurance company should perform. 2.Compulsory Scheme of Coverage It is our opinion that the most feasible business model is to make the program compulsory. The compulsory nature of the scheme has the advantages of having the economies of scale, broader coverage, anti-selection avoidance, and project sustainability. The compulsory scheme should be done thru legislation and shall be decided upon Congress. The legislation must specify: a) Agency to enforce catastrophe insurance requirement; b) Specific risks covered like flood, earthquake, tornado, typhoon and tsunami; c) Evaluation of premium by the Insurance commission; d) The covered persons or companies like the small and medium enterprises; e) Any share on the premium by the government; f) Tax exemption on the insurance product; g) Governance structure; h) Representation by government agencies; and i) Participation of the local insurers in the company. The PCIP should not rely only on the mandatory coverage of properties as required ; by law or regulation, but must strive to be self-sustaining through proper underwriting, reinsurance, and Joss ratio management among other aspects of operation. 3.Premium Rating The Commission shall be involved in reviewing the premium of the coverage. 4.Capitalization We agree to the proposed Php. 2 billion initial capital of PCIP and Its subsequent increase to Php 3.5 billion. The proposal is silent as to the source of the initial capital that will fund the operation of the insurance pool. In case it is a mutual Insurance company, policyholders might have difficulty in the required amount as members’ 2 a *s 1 , ° . ° equity of the insurance pool at the initial stage of the operation. * 5, Use of Parametric Trigger We agree on the use of parametric trigger for immediate payment of the portion of the loss and to adopt actual loss evaluation and documentation for losses beyond the agreed limit or percentage. We support the use of reliable data from the local and foreign government agencies in determining the actual index or providing parametric data as basis for payment of the loss or claim. The data must be available publicly and confirmation or certification should be available to the public. As much as possible, two providers of parametric data could be used or relied upon. The use of other cost-efficient and reliable technology like the use of remote sensing technology and Image data from drone should be promoted to minimize or do away with the actual inspection of the adjuster. 6. Public Relations We agree to the conduct of public relation activities to jumpstart support and public awareness of the catastrophe insurance program. 7. Disclosure Consumer protection should be paramount in the implementation of the program. Enough disclosure should be given to the clients prior to the issuance of the policy, ‘ which shall include the amount of premium, term of renewal, claims processes and 4 requirement, salient conditions of the policy, status of reinsurance, and participation | in declsion-making. The concept of parametric insurance should be explained or communicated properly to clients to avoid confusion in its application. The parametric data shall be made available In the website of the PCIP and the agency providing the parametric data. | &. Reports Annual report of the PCIP shall be submitted to the Insurance Commission and be made available in the website of the PCIP. 9. Distribution We agree that the distribution of the insurance policies shall be done to the , accredited local insurance companies, including the functions of premium collection and claims settlement. 10. Claims Limit We suggest that a limit for claims per catastrophic event shall be provided in the policy to maintain the sustainability of the program. 3 11. Insurance Companies ) The insurance companies shall be part owners or shareholders of the PCIP to give them greater interest in the success of the corporation and to share their expertise in the administration of the PCIP. : Thank you very much for allowing us to comment on the proposed catastrophe insurance scheme and we look forward to more collaboration for the refinement of the program and its implementation that will provide financial help to Filipinos in case , of the happening of a catastrophic event. : Very trul¥ yours, D .
